title: Filament Drybox Humidity Exposure Risk
dataSources: Print jobs (`octoprint:job`), printer telemetry (`printer:telemetry`), Klipper resonance metrics (`klipper:telemetry`), resin print logs (`resinprint:job`), tool usage (`tool:usage`), filament inventory (`filament:spool`), and workshop air readings (`workshop:air`).
app: Maker telemetry from OctoPrint, Moonraker, printer firmware sensors, resin printer job logs, smart dryboxes, and workshop tool sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool
| stats latest(drybox_rh_pct) as drybox_rh_pct latest(spool_grams_remaining) as grams_remaining by spool material
| where drybox_rh_pct>30
| sort - drybox_rh_pct
description: Flags spools sitting in overly humid dryboxes so brittle prints and popping filament do not arrive as a surprise.
value: Filament condition degrades quietly, and humidity exposure is an easy metric to watch before quality problems spread across multiple jobs.
implementation: Stream humidity from each drybox and associate every active spool with its storage location and remaining weight.
visualization: Table of spools at risk from elevated drybox humidity.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Making, 3D Printing & Workshop — typical feeds: Print jobs (`octoprint:job`), printer firmware telemetry (`printer:telemetry`), filament spools (`filament:spool`), CNC/laser jobs (`cnc:job`), workshop air (`workshop:air`), cordless tool batteries (.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `filament:spool`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=filament:spool`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** OctoPrint / Klipper (Moonraker) print servers, printer firmware telemetry, filament spool tracking, CNC/laser job logs, and workshop air/tool sensors via HEC and MQTT..

**Author notes:** Stream humidity from each drybox and associate every active spool with its storage location and remaining weight.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "filament:spool", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Filament Drybox Humidity Exposure Risk** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=filament:spool`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `drybox_rh_pct` (> 30) after latest — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `drybox_rh_pct`, `material`, `spool`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool
| stats latest(drybox_rh_pct) as drybox_rh_pct latest(spool_grams_remaining) as grams_remaining by spool material
| where drybox_rh_pct>30
| sort - drybox_rh_pct
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table drybox_rh_pct, material, spool
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `drybox_rh_pct` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(drybox_rh_pct) AS p50 perc90(drybox_rh_pct) AS p90 perc99(drybox_rh_pct) AS p99 max(drybox_rh_pct) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.17.18: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Spools At Risk From Elevated Drybox Humidity (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `filament:spool` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=filament:spool | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
